job.title: Global Head of Growth
job.description:
• Leading regulatory growth consultancy and B2C technology start up 
  • Own the entire marketing growth engine of an existing powerhouse and new tech platform.
  • C-suite scale up opportunity, backed by a reputable brand 


About the organisation

This well-established, leading Australian-backed company is launching a new software platform that helps entrepreneurs start, run and grow businesses in regulated industries. By bringing business setup, licensing, compliance and growth tools into one place, the platform makes business ownership more accessible in markets traditionally difficult to enter, creating a significant opportunity for global expansion. With ambitious plans to establish a differentiated market position, build a recognised brand and expand globally, the organisation is entering an exciting phase of growth. This is an opportunity to join at a pivotal stage, shape the future direction of a new platform (and the existing company) and play a defining role in building a high-growth global technology platform. 


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and indirectly to the Founder & CEO, the Global Head of Growth will own the end-to-end marketing growth strategy, with primary accountability for launching and scaling the new platform, as well as leading the company's existing marketing function. This is a strategic, commercially accountable leadership role spanning the entire customer journey, from market awareness and acquisition through to conversion, activation, engagement and retention. You will design and build the growth engine, encompassing paid and organic acquisition, funnel optimisation, lifecycle marketing, CRM, automation and customer experience. You will also shape brand positioning, messaging and category creation, establishing a compelling market narrative and creative direction across paid, organic, social and video channels. Leading a multidisciplinary team across campaigns, lifecycle, performance, social, video and PR, you will establish a high-performance growth culture, drive data-led decision-making and ensure marketing investment translates into measurable commercial outcomes. You will own analytics, attribution and performance reporting, bringing together strategic leadership with a hands-on approach to execution. This is fundamentally a builder role. The opportunity is to establish a scalable, commercially accountable growth engine, create repeatable acquisition and retention models, and develop the platform's presence in Australia and international markets.  


About you

You are an accomplished B2C growth and marketing leader with a track record of building and scaling businesses in high-growth, performance-driven technology and/or large consumer branded product environments. You have been instrumental in taking a product, platform or brand from early-stage through to meaningful commercial scale, ideally within a technology, SaaS, digital platform or high-profile consumer business. Your experience combines strong B2C acquisition and brand-building capabilities with an understanding of B2B customer acquisition and commercial models. You have owned end-to-end growth strategies, including acquisition funnels, performance marketing, lifecycle, CRM, retention and brand positioning. You are equally comfortable developing a growth strategy, managing significant advertising budgets, analysing conversion data and rolling up your sleeves to execute. An experienced leader of multidisciplinary teams, you know how to build capability, establish accountability and create a culture of high performance and continuous improvement. You bring strong commercial acumen, analytical capability and a deep understanding of digital customer behaviour. Fluent in performance marketing, CRM, automation and emerging AI-enabled marketing tools, you have a strong appreciation for brand, creative and compelling storytelling. Above all, you are entrepreneurial, commercially driven and comfortable operating in an evolving environment. You thrive on building something from the ground up, move quickly from strategy to execution and have the ambition to take a new technology platform into new markets.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Tracy Melonie at SHK via email at tracy.melonie@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3705468. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Group Manager, Enterprise Technology & Digital Enablement
job.description:
• Set enterprise technology direction
  • Shape technology in a commercially focused state agency
  • Foster business engagement and a high performing team


About the organisation

VicTrack owns Victoria’s rail land, infrastructure, and related assets, with an $88 billion portfolio. In addition to its ongoing asset custodian role, the organisation is transforming to be a more commercially driven business, pursuing new opportunities from its extensive asset base and strengthening its core role in Victoria’s transport system. With annual revenue at around $150 million and ambitions for significant growth, VicTrack is reshaping how it operates to meet its aspirations for the future.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Enterprise Services Officer and sitting on the Enterprise Services Senior Leadership Team, you will be VicTrack’s most senior technology leader. You will be accountable for technology, digital capability, data management and cyber security across the internal operating environment, leading a team of approximately 30 spanning strategy and architecture, portfolio and business engagement, program delivery, enterprise applications, digital enablement, and technology operations and security. You will develop an enterprise strategy, a three-year integrated roadmap and costed annual plans, and establish transparent investment and portfolio governance, all while maintaining secure, resilient operations across critical infrastructure and telecommunications assets. You will also lead implementation of the future state operating model, reshape team capability and enable the responsible adoption of automation, data and AI. Key to success will be building business engagement and trust, and translating technology, commercial and risk matters into clear advice that supports investment decisions by the Executive Leadership Team and Board.


About you

You are a highly engaging senior technology executive with substantial experience leading enterprise technology and digital functions in complex, asset intensive, regulated or public purpose environments. Tertiary qualified, you have some direct prior experience in government, while bringing a well-tuned commercial mindset, with experience managing significant budgets, strategic sourcing, major vendor relationships and commercial contracts. You have governed cyber security, operational resilience and risk at enterprise level, and understand the obligations that come with critical infrastructure. You have led teams through change with openness, respect and emotional intelligence, and take calculated risks with sound judgement. As a member of a senior leadership group, you influence peers, executives and Boards, and hold your position constructively. Experience in transport, infrastructure or telecommunications will be advantageous. Motivated by VicTrack’s purpose, you want to build technology foundations that create lasting impact.


How to apply

For more information see the Candidate brief Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Brian at SHK via email at brian.barry@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3707317 (do not email your CV). Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. NOTE: Applicants must hold full Australian working rights to be considered for this position.

job.title: Executive Director, Transformation and Reform
job.description:
• Lead whole-of-enterprise transformation
  • Expanded powers and jurisdiction
  • Strengthen anti-corruption measures


About the organisation

The Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission (IBAC) works to expose and prevent corruption affecting all Victorians. Recent legislative reform has expanded IBAC's powers and jurisdiction, which requires new and strengthened capabilities. The organisation is focused on meeting those obligations, guided by the IBAC Strategy 2025–28 and a focus on responsiveness, enabling intelligence and people. IBAC's Executive Leadership Team works to a leadership charter built on mutual support and open discussion, with decisions made in the interests of the whole organisation.


About the role

A new role reporting to the CEO and sitting on the Executive Leadership Team, the Executive Director, Transformation and Reform will lead the enterprise-wide transformation of IBAC. The Executive Director will create the future-state vision and integrated roadmap, work with the CEO on the operating model redesign and personally lead the reform workstreams around it, from concept to delivery. The role will also establish and lead a small team, collaborate with and advise the executive on priorities, risks and trade-offs, and help develop new capabilities alongside the uplift of the existing skillsets. Key to success will be maintaining statutory functions throughout and handing reform outcomes to business owners with sustainable capability in place. This is a two-year fixed-term appointment.


About you

You are an accomplished executive who has led complex, organisation-wide transformation from strategy to implementation in public sector integrity, regulatory, compliance, investigative or oversight environments. You bring a deep understanding of government and its accountability frameworks, enabling you to deliver meaningful, sustainable change while maintaining operational effectiveness. Pragmatic and future-focused, you can navigate legal and statutory complexity, connect strategy with execution, and keep people engaged through change. You are a collaborative and trusted leader who values different perspectives, builds genuine partnerships, and contributes positively to executive decision-making. Motivated by public purpose, you will relish the opportunity to help shape IBAC’s future and strengthen confidence in Victoria’s integrity system.


How to apply

For more information see the Candidate Brief. Click ‘Apply Now’ (above) to submit your CV along with a covering letter (1 page) or contact Matthew Belleghem at SHK via email on matthew.belleghem@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3700161. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Closes 22 November, 11.59pm.

job.title: Director, Compliance Monitoring & Sanctions
job.description:
• Lead statewide compliance and sanctions
  • Victoria's independent environmental regulator
  • Prevent pollution and waste harm


About the organisation

Environment Protection Authority Victoria (EPA) is the state's environmental regulator, working to prevent and reduce the harmful effects of pollution and waste on Victorian communities and ecosystems. Operating under a strong legislative mandate and a science-based approach, EPA partners with government, industry and the public to protect the environment and human health. This organisation is values-led, future-focused, and committed to delivering lasting impact for all Victorians.

 

About the role

As the Director, you will lead EPA's statewide compliance monitoring and sanctions functions and guide its frontline regulatory workforce. You will ensure that regulatory actions, decisions and sanctions including  inspections notices, compliance advice, infringements, and official warnings, are consistent and proportionate across Victoria, in line with EPA's Compliance and Enforcement Policy. Reporting to the Executive Director, Regulatory Operations and Sector Regulation and leading a large and diverse team based across the state, you will set standards for regulatory practice, decision-making and performance, and oversee planning, budgets and workforce capability. As a leadership team member, you will advise the CEO and Senior Executive Committee on regulatory risk, enforcement and operational performance. Success will mean robust relationships with government, co-regulators and internal and external stakeholders, and regular travel across metropolitan and regional Victoria to stay connected to frontline work.

 

About you

You are an experienced senior regulatory leader who has led large, complex compliance, enforcement or sanctions functions at executive level in government or a comparable regulatory environment. You understand environmental regulation and use regulatory and sanctions tools effectively, ideally supported by tertiary qualifications in science, law, environmental management, public policy or a related discipline. You have led dispersed frontline teams, strengthened consistency and performance, and delivered organisational change. You bring sound judgement to sensitive regulatory matters, influence senior stakeholders and represent EPA credibly with government, industry and the community. You build teams that take pride in their work and responsibility for their decisions. Your leadership will help turn fair, consistent regulation into stronger protection for Victoria's communities and environment.


How to apply

For more information, please review the Candidate Brief, then click ‘apply now’ above to submit your CV/resume and a concise cover letter. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Closes 16 November.

This organisation is values-led, future-focused, and committed to delivering lasting impact for all Victorians.


About the role

About you

You are an experienced executive leader with sound judgement on complex regulatory, environmental and public policy matters. You strengthen governance, manage risk, make robust, consistent decisions, and have led change and reform. You build trusted relationships with peers, senior government, industry and community stakeholders, give executives and ministers clear, evidence-based advice, and manage resources, performance and investment for lasting outcomes. job.title: Executive General Manager Women’s Safety, Youth & Family Services
job.description:
• National executive leadership role within a purpose-driven organisation
  • Drive impact across women's safety, youth and family services
  • Lead at the intersection of service delivery, policy and social impact


About the organisation

Good Shepherd Australia New Zealand is a leading social purpose organisation dedicated to supporting women, girls and families to be safe, well, strong and connected. With a heritage spanning more than 160 years, Good Shepherd works across family violence, youth and family services, financial wellbeing, housing and community development, combining direct service delivery with advocacy, research and partnerships to address disadvantage and create opportunities for people to thrive. Guided by its commitment to dignity, equity and social justice, Good Shepherd operates across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand and continues to play an influential role in shaping responses to some of the most significant social challenges facing communities today.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Executive General Manager, Women's Safety, Youth & Family Services will lead a substantial portfolio supporting women, children, young people and families across a diverse range of programs and services. The role operates at the intersection of service delivery, government policy, sector reform and community need, requiring leadership across a complex stakeholder, funding and regulatory environment. The appointee will be responsible for strengthening organisational performance, service quality, workforce capability and sustainable outcomes while navigating increasing demand, evolving community expectations and a changing policy landscape. Working closely with government, community organisations and sector stakeholders, the position will contribute to the delivery of Good Shepherd's strategic priorities and help ensure the organisation remains responsive to emerging challenges and opportunities, identifying emerging needs and developing innovative solutions. Additionally, the EGM provides specialist knowledge across the organisation and the Good Shepherd network in Australia and internationally. 


About you

You are an accomplished executive with experience leading complex service organisations within community services, family services, family violence, health, human services or adjacent purpose-driven sectors. You have successfully led large and diverse teams, delivered operational and financial performance, and navigated complex stakeholder environments. Commercially astute and strategically minded, you bring strong leadership capability together with experience building productive relationships across government, community and sector networks. Most importantly, you are a values-led leader whose integrity, judgement and collaborative approach enable you to build high-performing teams and deliver meaningful outcomes for communities. You will also demonstrate a humble and collaborative approach to working with Executive colleagues and their teams. This is a rare opportunity to lead at scale while contributing to an organisation with a long history of community impact, advocacy and innovation


How to apply

Closing date for receipt of applications is November 15, 2026. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Network General Manager - Finance, Budget and Audit
job.description:
• Regional finance leadership role within a purpose-driven organisation
  • Drive impact across women's safety, youth and family services
  • Lead financial stewardship, audit and governance across a complex network


About the organisation

Good Shepherd Australia New Zealand (GSANZ) is a leading social purpose organisation dedicated to supporting women, girls and families to be safe, well, strong and connected. With a heritage spanning more than 160 years, Good Shepherd works across family violence, youth and family services, financial wellbeing, housing and community development, combining direct service delivery with advocacy, research and partnerships to address disadvantage and create opportunities for people to thrive. Guided by its commitment to dignity, equity and social justice, Good Shepherd operates across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand and continues to play an influential role in shaping responses to some of the most significant social challenges facing communities today.


About the role

Reporting to the Executive General Manager – Finance, Investment and Risk, the Network General Manager – Finance, Budget and Audit is a member of the Senior Leadership Team. The role provides enterprise leadership for financial stewardship, budgeting, audit readiness and financial governance across GSANZ, including its New Zealand entities and the Sisters of the Good Shepherd. The Network General Manager will lead financial planning and statutory and management reporting, and will advise the CEO, Executive Leadership Team, Board and Board Committees. The appointee will oversee cash flow, liquidity, investments, accounts payable and receivable, fundraising, payroll and procurement, as well as management of auditors, banking, insurance and investment adviser relationships. Key to success will be strengthening the finance operating model, enhancing ERP and reporting capability, and delivering strategic improvements to payroll operations through the successful insourcing of the payroll function.


About you

CA/CPA qualified, you are an accomplished senior finance professional with significant leadership experience in purpose-led organisations across social impact, community, health, education or regulated sectors. You have successfully led budgeting, reporting, audit and control functions across geographic, structural and systems complexity, and you confidently advise Boards and executives with clarity, insight and perspective. Commercially astute and strategically minded, you bring strong leadership capability together with experience building productive relationships. You have successfully led teams through change, driven continuous improvement initiatives and built high-performing, values-aligned finance functions. Familiarity with New Zealand financial and regulatory settings will be well regarded, as will an understanding of government funding, philanthropic partnerships, community housing and payroll systems. With emotional intelligence, humility and professional maturity, you operate with authenticity, foster trust, and navigate complex conversations constructively, while remaining aligned to the organisation's mission and values.


How to apply

job.title: Senior Manager, Trusts & Foundations
job.description:
• Nobel Prize-winning medical research institute
  • Lead a significant philanthropic portfolio
  • Turn philanthropy into life-changing discoveries


About the organisation

WEHI (Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research) is a medical research institute in Melbourne's Parkville biomedical precinct, with more than 80 faculties and over 1,400 staff and students. Its research covers cancer, infection, inflammation, immune disorders, and developmental and degenerative diseases, from fundamental molecular and cellular discovery through to new medicines and diagnostics. The institute's researchers have received the Nobel Prize and Lasker Awards, and its discoveries have contributed to vaccines, growth factors, blood stem cell transplantation and novel anti-cancer treatments. Philanthropy provides approximately 25% of WEHI's annual budget and supports the recruitment and retention of leading scientists. Recent senior appointments in immunology, cancer and fundamental biology are creating new funding opportunities for the organisation.


About the role

Reporting to and working closely with the Chief Development Officer, the Senior Manager Trusts & Foundations leads one of WEHI’s most significant and strategically important fundraising portfolios, playing a pivotal role in securing philanthropic investment to advance world-leading medical research. The Senior Manager will steward and report to an established base of funders, protect and retain revenue, and expand the program nationally and internationally beyond its current Melbourne focus. This includes building the pipeline from identification and cultivation through to EOIs and proposals, turning complex science into clear funding propositions, and representing WEHI to major global foundations. The role works closely with science leads, deputy directors, strategy, finance and the Grants & Major Bids team, which partners on pre- and post-award management. Key to success in the first six months will be re-establishing business as usual while identifying efficiencies and untapped funding opportunities, supported by sound governance and a highly supportive team.


About you

Tertiary qualified, you are a trusts and foundations specialist with substantial experience identifying, cultivating, soliciting and managing funder relationships and applications. You write exceptionally well and can translate technical content into plain language, while retaining scientific credibility. You have the seniority to represent WEHI to the world's largest foundations. You also have the judgement and negotiation skills to work with shared service teams, influence senior internal stakeholders and hold researchers to deadlines. As an experienced people leader, you develop others, set clear standards and use data to manage pipeline, performance and risk. Experience in health, medical research or higher education, a scientific background, and Raiser's Edge proficiency will be highly regarded.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Kylie Kilmartin at SHK on 0401 167 433 or via email at kylie.kilmartin@shk.com.au. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Board Member | Chair of the Board
job.description:
• Non-executive Board leadership role
  • Statewide youth charity since 1976
  • Improve outcomes for young people


About the organisation

Blue Light Victoria (BLV) is a statewide youth charity focused on early intervention and prevention for young people aged 10 to 21. Founded in 1976 commencing with drug- and alcohol-free youth discos, BLV now delivers programs and initiatives to more than 10,000 young people each year. BLV's evidence-based, trauma-informed programs bring young people together with police, emergency services, schools and communities to strengthen belonging, build trusted relationships, improve wellbeing and create safer, stronger communities. The charity is distinguished by its partnerships with police and emergency services, and is guided by the values of Connection, Growth, Innovation and Respect. BLV is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion and child safety.


About the role

BLV is seeking a Director with the capability and aspiration to contribute to the leadership of the Board, with the opportunity to assume the Chair role either on appointment or as part of future Board succession. As a Board member you will contribute to the Board's governance of BLV and its oversight of strategy, organisational performance, impact, financial sustainability and risk, while maintaining clear boundaries between governance and management. For a candidate appointed as Chair, or transitioning to the Chair role in the future, responsibilities will include chairing Board and member meetings, setting agendas with the CEO and Secretary, working with the Deputy Chair on continuity and succession, and leading Board and Director evaluation, renewal and development. The Chair also acts as the primary point of contact between the Board and CEO, leading CEO appointment, goal-setting, performance evaluation, remuneration review and succession planning on behalf of the Board. As a Director, you will also play an important role in representing BLV and strengthening relationships with Victoria Police, government, schools, community partners, funders, donors, branches and volunteers, with a sustained focus on child safety, youth voice, diversity, equity and inclusion. The Director position is a voluntary, non-executive, appointment for a term of up to 3 years, and Chair is for 12 months with eligibility for reappointment at each Annual General Meeting


About you

You are a senior leader with substantial governance experience and a sound understanding of the role and responsibilities of a non-executive Director. Previous Board experience is highly desirable, as is completion of the AICD Company Directors Course or an equivalent governance qualification. You may already have Chair experience or be ready to step into a Chair role, either on appointment or as part of future Board succession planning. You bring strong strategic judgement, financial literacy and an understanding of governance, risk and regulatory oversight, with the ability to assess complex information and guide collective decision-making. Your well-established networks and natural ability to connect people with purpose, will help BLV broaden its funding beyond government sources and support its long-term sustainability. Underpinning your ability to support and work constructively with a CEO and maintain appropriate boundaries between the Board, Chair and CEO, is important, as are your independence, integrity and confidence to challenge constructively. You hold a genuine commitment to BLV's purpose, values, child safety and improving outcomes for young people

 

How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Dalia Klein at SHK on 0401 000 499, quoting reference 3693460. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Advancement Programs Director
job.description:
• Leading global university 
  • Shape the future of alumni and donor engagement
  • Build loyalty at scale


About the organisation

UNSW Sydney is a globally connected university with more than 400,000 alumni and a donor community of approximately 25,000. Its strategy, Progress for All, sets an ambitious agenda for creating positive societal impact through education, research and meaningful engagement with its communities and partners. Following a refreshed Advancement strategy, UNSW has created this new role to bring greater strategic coherence to how it engages alumni, donors and supporters throughout their relationship with the University. This is an opportunity to help shape the next phase of an ambitious Advancement function at one of Australia’s leading universities, applying contemporary thinking in loyalty, customer experience, data and lifecycle engagement to a purpose-led organisation with significant scale and impact.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, and leading a team, the Advancement Programs Director is a key member of the Advancement leadership team, working alongside the Directors of Development, Alumni Experience and Advancement Services to shape a more connected and insight-led approach to alumni and donor engagement. 

The Director will provide strategic leadership for supporter journeys, lifecycle engagement and development communications, including community giving. A central focus will be understanding how different audiences move through the advancement ecosystem, from alumni engagement and community giving through to major and principal gifts, and designing more connected, purposeful experiences along the journey. 

The role will establish the strategies, frameworks and standards that enable consistent communications, events, stewardship and supporter experiences. Working in partnership with Advancement Services, the Director will define the segmentation, data, reporting and insights required to understand audience behaviour, evaluate performance and improvement engagement over time. 

The Director will also represent Advancement audiences and priorities to central marketing, digital and communications teams and senior University leaders. A key early priority will be developing a clear first-year strategy that maps audiences and cohorts, identifies the journeys and experiences required, establishes clear priorities and makes a compelling case for future investment.


About you

Tertiary qualified, you are a senior customer, marketing, or engagement leader with deep expertise in lifecycle strategy, loyalty or CRM-driven engagement, gained in complex organisations. Higher education or philanthropy experience is not essential. You understand how data, insight and customer behaviour can be translated into more meaningful engagement and measurable results. You bring a strong point of view on best practice, can distinguish between what is strategically important and what is simply possible, and are confident setting priorities, including being clear about what not to pursue. You have experience leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing across marketing, digital and data specialists while bringing stakeholders with you through change. You are comfortable operating across a complex institution, building a case for investment and translating strategy into practical action.

You bring curiosity and commercial judgement, along with the confidence to build something new in an environment where ambiguity, competing priorities and limited resources are part of the landscape. What matters is your ability to understand audiences, connect data and experience, build effective strategies and create the conditions for long-term engagement.

Most importantly, you will be excited by the opportunity to build something new and establish the foundations for more connected alumni and donor engagement at scale. 


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Kylie Kilmartin at SHK on 0401 167 433 or via email at kylie.kilmartin@shk.com.au. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Manager, Philanthropy
job.description:
• One of Australia's most trusted charities
  • Lead a national major gifts team
  • Exciting transformational growth mandate


About the organisation

This organisation is one of Australia's most recognised and trusted charities operating nationally across every state and territory. With a broad footprint spanning social services, community support, and emergency relief, its operations touch every demographic and age group while also bringing hope to people experiencing hardship and injustice. The organisation serves people across all walks of life — from crisis support to long-term community development. A substantial fundraising operation, underpinned by a high-performing transformational giving team, has delivered consistent year-on-year growth and continues to play a critical role in advancing the organisation’s purpose. Through an integrated and holistic approach, it creates lasting spiritual and social change for individuals and families across Australia.


About the role

Reporting to the General Manager, Transformational Gifts, the Manager, Philanthropy plays a critical leadership role in advancing the organisation’s mission through the development of meaningful, high-value philanthropic relationships in line with the fundraising strategy. This position is responsible for driving sustainable income growth by identifying, cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major donors including securing seven-figure gifts, and building strong, long-term relationships with philanthropic stakeholders. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on relationship management, the appointee will ensure that philanthropic investment is aligned with organisational priorities and delivers measurable social impact. Collaborating with internal stakeholders to translate programmatic needs into compelling funding propositions, the appointee will build long-term partnerships grounded in trust, transparency and shared purpose, and through disciplined pipeline management, strong market intelligence, and exceptional donor engagement, contribute, to revenue diversification, multi-year funding security, and the overall growth of the philanthropy portfolio. The role is also responsible for achieving financial and non-financial targets, inspiring a national team that is tasked with acquiring new strategic relationships, and driving revenue growth and retention. Critical to success is building team capabilities and optimising ROI performance, while ensuring contemporary best practice processes. 


About you

You are an experienced philanthropy or major gifts leader with demonstrable experience securing seven-figure gifts. You bring leadership experience, ideally across a geographically dispersed team, and possess the commercial and strategic capability to manage a multi ten-million-dollar portfolio of philanthropic revenue. Your stakeholder management skills are well developed, and you present with the gravitas and executive presence required to engage ultra-high-net-worth individuals and their intermediaries. You have the ability to navigate a large complex organisation and to work collaboratively and collectively with this framework. You may come from a large charity, higher education, health or medical research, other relevant philanthropic sectors, or a high-net-worth relationship management background in wealth or private banking where your skills translate meaningfully into the welfare sector. You thrive on operating within a values-led, mission-driven organisation where you can meaningfully impact and transform people’s lives.


How to apply

The organisation serves people across all walks of life — from crisis support to long-term community development. A substantial fundraising operation, underpinned by a high-performing transformational giving team, has delivered consistent year-on-year growth and continues to play a critical role in advancing the organisation’s purpose. Through an integrated and holistic approach, it creates lasting spiritual and social change for individuals and families across Australia.


About the role

Reporting to the General Manager, Transformational Gifts, the Manager, Philanthropy plays a critical leadership role in advancing the organisation’s mission through the development of meaningful, high-value philanthropic relationships in line with the fundraising strategy. This position is responsible for driving sustainable income growth by identifying, cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major donors including securing seven-figure gifts, and building strong, long-term relationships with philanthropic stakeholders. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on relationship management, the appointee will ensure that philanthropic investment is aligned with organisational priorities and delivers measurable social impact. Collaborating with internal stakeholders to translate programmatic needs into compelling funding propositions, the appointee will build long-term partnerships grounded in trust, transparency and shared purpose, and through disciplined pipeline management, strong market intelligence, and exceptional donor engagement, contribute, to revenue diversification, multi-year funding security, and the overall growth of the philanthropy portfolio. The role is also responsible for achieving financial and non-financial targets, inspiring a national team that is tasked with acquiring new strategic relationships, and driving revenue growth and retention. Critical to success is building team capabilities and optimising ROI performance, while ensuring contemporary best practice processes. 


About you

You are an experienced philanthropy or major gifts leader with demonstrable experience securing seven-figure gifts. You bring leadership experience, ideally across a geographically dispersed team, and possess the commercial and strategic capability to manage a multi ten-million-dollar portfolio of philanthropic revenue. Your stakeholder management skills are well developed, and you present with the gravitas and executive presence required to engage ultra-high-net-worth individuals and their intermediaries. You have the ability to navigate a large complex organisation and to work collaboratively and collectively with this framework. You may come from a large charity, higher education, health or medical research, other relevant philanthropic sectors, or a high-net-worth relationship management background in wealth or private banking where your skills translate meaningfully into the welfare sector. You thrive on operating within a values-led, mission-driven organisation where you can meaningfully impact and transform people’s lives.
